item.title: The Forgotten First Schoolteacher in Kasilof — Part 1
item.description: AUTHOR’S NOTE: On Sept. 25, 2025, Brent Johnson, one of the most authoritative voices on the history of the Kasilof and Cohoe areas on the Kenai Peninsula, sent me screenshots from two 1929 Illinois newspaper articles. He appended to the attachments this note: “Prior to seeing these newspaper articles, I was pretty confident that Enid McLane was Kasilof’s first teacher and that the first school year was 1932-33. The school building McLane used was owned by Abram Erickson near the [Gust] Ness homestead on the Cohoe side of the [Kasilof] river.” But if the exceedingly brief 1929 newspaper excerpts were correct, Brent found himself suddenly left with questions he hadn’t pondered before — about the location of a Kasilof school prior to 1932, about the number of students in that school, and, most importantly, about the identity of the teacher mentioned in one of the articles. That one-sentence article, from the Lake County (Illinois) Register on May 8, 1929, read: “Mrs. Neil Brown Sr. is teaching in Kasilof, Alaska, where the Brown family moved from Deerfield last year.”
